Subject: Next steps: Lumina integration pilot — Python/TS quickstart & local test checklist

Thanks again for the call today, Devin — great to learn more about the search + triage workflow at Lumina. Quick recap (so we all have the same list) and proposed next steps for the pilot: 

Recap (what you told us)
- Goal: replace current keyword search with embeddings + reranker for clinician notes and post-visit triage (SLA: <200ms p99 for interactive UI).
- Primary constraints: VPC-only deployment, KMS-managed keys, current infra on EKS (AWS), and strict data retention rules.
- Desired features: structured output for routing (JSON schema), ability to call internal tools (e.g., patient-status lookup), and a fallback to smaller model on spikes.

Technical asks we agreed to (pilot scope)
1) SDK quickstart for both Python and TypeScript (local dev + containerized run)
2) Auth patterns: API key in dev, signed requests + KMS integration for prod credentials
3) Embeddings + reranker sample (indexing small sample set, rerank flow)
4) Local testing guide (M1/M2 laptop, plus Docker fallback)
5) Security questionnaire + SOC2/attestation pointers for procurement

Attachments & links I uploaded: redwood_env_checklist_v1.pdf (env & network checklist) and redwood_quickstart_links.txt (links to sample repos & gists). Also putting the quick GitHub and Drive links below.

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline)
- Today: I’ll send the quickstart links, the env checklist, and a short local test guide. (attached)
- Early next week: 30-min technical sandbox session with Marissa + Dev to walk through auth and routing choices (please suggest times).
- Before pilot: a short mutual action plan (MAP) doc that lists success metrics and acceptance criteria.

Questions I have for you (so we can tailor the quickstart)
- Can dev machines use a VPN into your VPC for testing, or will you prefer a narrow proxy access pattern?
- Any hard tokenization/PII redaction policies we should bake into the sample data?

Links and resources (attached)
- GitHub quickstarts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/tree/main/lumina-python-ts
- Lumina pilot Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-shared-drive/lumina-pilot-resources

If that looks right, I’ll send the short local guide + a scheduling poll for the tech session. Thanks — looking forward to getting you set up.

Great questions — answers inline and a few code pointers below. Attaching a short local_test_guide.md that includes commands.

Local/M1 notes
- Most quickstarts are written to run with Docker for reproducibility, but we include native Apple Silicon wheels where available. For embeddings and small dev models you should be able to run locally on M1/M2; the guide includes a fallback Docker command.

Auth pattern (recommended for pilot)
1) Dev: API key in environment (REDWOOD_API_KEY) for quickstart.
2) Prod-demo: short-lived signing token approach — client exchanges mTLS-authenticated assertion with your KMS, KMS returns a short-lived credential that the SDK accepts.
3) We’ll provide an example that shows signing a payload (HMAC) and how to configure the SDK to use a KMS-wrapped key.

Example (Python) — minimal auth flow (pseudo):
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_…
- python quickstart/sample_infer.py --model small --input-file test.json

Example (TypeScript) — minimal auth (pseudo):
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_... node quickstart/ts/run.js

Routing & structured output
- Suggest using per-route policies in the SDK: route by latency SLO for interactive UI (route->small-quant model) and by cost for batch jobs. The sample app shows how to request structured JSON output and validate against a schema before tool-calling.

Embeddings & reranker notes
- Yes, we support batching at index-time; quickstart includes a small script (index_batch.py / index_batch.ts) that batches at 128 vectors.
- For reranking you can either call Redwood’s reranker endpoint post-vector-retrieval, or host a lightweight reranker function in your app that calls the Redwood model. We include a Pinecone example in the repo.

Security artifacts & procurement
- I attached a stubbed security packet (redwood_security_packet_stub.txt) in the Drive folder and a short list of artifacts we can provide: SOC2 type II summary, data flow diagrams, encryption whitepaper, and an audit log sample. For legal/procurement questions, loop in procurement@redwoodinference.com — I’m copying Marissa who can own the procurement packet.

Scheduling
- Suggested 30-min slots: Mon 6/15 10:00–10:30 or Tue 6/16 14:00–14:30 ET. Pick one and we’ll send a calendar invite.

- Local test guide (attached): local_test_guide.md
